# Vendored third-party trees

Plain-tree vendored copies (not submodules). **Never edit vendored code** —
portability/build issues are handled from the top-level CMakeLists (target
scoping, options, the pkg-config shim), not by patching. To update, re-copy a
newer tree and update the provenance below.

| tree | upstream | vendored commit | copied from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `devourer/` | https://github.com/OpenIPC/devourer | `f86f92d` (#402–#408) | Plain-tree copy of upstream `master`; `reference/` and `.gitmodules` excluded. No local vendor delta. This includes the upstreamed RTL8822E MCS4+/48M+ TX, `0x41e8` RX-desense, eFEM/DPDT, calibration/runtime, and channel-switch fixes from `b5a6df7` (#238/#268), superseding the former `snokvist/devourer` cherry-pick pin; the per-unit EFUSE MAC identity (`IRtlDevice::GetPermanentMacAddress`, #383/#386) and the Jaguar3 EFUSE-walk append-order fix (#384 — flips 8822C `rfe_type` 0→3, a 7-RF-register delta; CU bench re-baselined, see `docs/findings.md` 2026-08-07); the RTL8733BU monitor RX / raw TX backend (#388) and its `FastRetune` port (#398, 345→55 ms per hop). The `5bf059a` bump adds the **RTL8733BU §10.5 TX-power actuator** (#399) — `GetTxPowerCaps().supported` flips false→true on that family, which is all `io/src/air_radio.cpp`'s `power_actuator_ok` reads, so the §10.5 announce and the §10.6/§10.7 calibration refusal self-enable with no consumer change. The `d2120b4` bump adds the **RTL8733BU USB TX aggregation port** (#400, merged as `52c6549`) — `send_packets` packs up to 3 `[txdesc][frame]` blocks per bulk-OUT URB, which is what `air.usb_tx_agg` + `RadioAir::inject_staged` exist to drive. Unlike the `5bf059a` bump this one is **not** self-enabling: `cfg.tx.usb_agg_max` defaults to 0 and the per-frame path stays byte-identical until a profile opts in. It also picks up **#401** (`d2120b4`), the maintainer's follow-up from #400's review: `bulk_send_sync_ep` returns *bytes submitted*, so `rc >= 0` also matched a short write, and Jaguar2/Jaguar3 counted those as delivered on BOTH their single-frame and aggregated paths. Both now require a full write, matching the 8733B and Kestrel. That reaches us: on 8812CU/EU `send_packet` now returns false where it returned true, which is what `RadioAir::inject` already treats as not-sent — strictly better accounting, and unreachable in practice besides (`UsbTransport::tx_sync` returns negative on every libusb error including timeout, so `0 <= rc < len` needs libusb to report success on a partial bulk-OUT). The 8733B's own delta is log-only: a hard transport failure now reaches stderr instead of only a short write. This row previously pinned #400's PR head; issue #215 owned the re-pin and is closed by it. The `f86f92d` bump adds the **RTL8733BU hardware-ARQ surface** (#406, #407) and its narrowband qualification (#403), plus RF characterization that is tests/docs only (#402, #404, #408). Three caps flip false→true on that family alone: `ack_responder_ok`, `tx_retry_limit_ok` and `narrowband_ok`, and `bw_mask_for_generation` gains `kBw10` (5 MHz is explicitly refused — that die's BB small-BW mode airs no packets). Like #399 and unlike #400 these are read by code we already ship, but the only consumer is a **refusal** that now stops firing: `air_radio.cpp`'s §3.0 Pass 156 leg rejects `return.unicast` on a TX die with `tx_retry_limit_ok=false`, so an 8733BU elected as the uplink can now carry unicast returns where it previously refused to start. Nothing self-arms — `air.ack_responder` still defaults off. The contract change reaching the fleet dies is `SetAckResponder` on Jaguar1/2/3: it now rejects a non-unicast MAC and **propagates the write's transport status** (`ack::enable` became `bool`), returning false where it used to `return true` unconditionally, and `ClearAckResponder` uses `disable_verified`. It is **not** a register readback — only the 8733B calls `ack::verify()`; upstream deliberately declines it on the Jaguar dies until each has a bench cell, since a family whose `0x0102` does not read back would start refusing healthy arms. The unicast gate can never fire against us: `kWbSaPrefix0` is `0x56` (`io/include/wblink/dot11.h:53`) and byte 0 is constant across net_id/originator/tx_idx, so `(mac[0] & 1) == 0` always. The status leg does reach us — `air_radio.cpp:529` treats false as the §3.0 loud-degrade leg and latches `ack_supported=false`, which `air_radio.cpp:310` documents as one-way — so a single transient control-write failure (500 ms `USB_TIMEOUT`) now reports the responder unsupported for the rest of the session on a craft that arms it, and `deploy/vehicle-192.168.2.232.json:89` is exactly that craft. The direction is honest (the old path reported a silently dead responder as armed) but the permanence is new. Against that, the bump **removes two uncaught-abort paths** the same craft was exposed to: old `ack::enable`/`disable` read `0x0102` through `ctrl_read`, which throws `std::ios_base::failure`, and both were `void` and unguarded, so a failed control read escaped `SetAckResponder` -> `arm_ack_responder` -> `RadioAir::create` with nothing catching it; both are `noexcept` with `catch(...)` now. #406 also makes devourer's own init throw when a configured `rx.ack_responder` cannot be armed; waybeam-link never sets that DeviceConfig field (it calls `SetAckResponder` directly after bring-up) and `DEVOURER_ACK_RESPONDER` is parsed only in an example TU that is never linked, so that path is unreachable from here. One NEW throw *is* reachable: `src/rtl8733b/Rtl8733bDevice.cpp:109` aborts bring-up when the `REG_ACKTO`/`REG_ACKTO_CCK` readback does not match the requested window, and we set `dc.tx.ack_timeout_us` on every adapter (`air_radio.cpp:1267`), so it runs on every 8733BU bring-up in the `x86-ground`, `rk3566` and `cv610` builds and is not caught around `InitWrite`. It joins seven throws already in that function, so the escape class is pre-existing rather than introduced here; device-verified latching on both fleet 8733BU units (a ground and the CV610 craft, each streaming >20 min on this pin). Optional Kestrel 11ax and non-fleet Jaguar families are forced off by the top-level CMake; waybeam-link builds 8812AU/CU/EU and RTL8733BU (`WBLINK_DEVOURER_CHIPS`) and enables only the devourer features it explicitly configures. |
| `libusb-cmake/` | https://github.com/libusb/libusb-cmake | `c8477c1` (includes the `libusb/` sources) | same Android checkout |
| `nlohmann/` | https://github.com/nlohmann/json | 3.12.0 single-header | (io layer only — core stays zero-dep) |

Build integration (top-level `CMakeLists.txt`, `WBLINK_RADIO=ON`):
- libusb is built static from `libusb-cmake` (examples/tests off, udev off —
  we never hotplug; the SSC338Q cross toolchain has no libudev).
- devourer's `pkg_check_modules(libusb-1.0)` is satisfied by
  `cmake/pkgconf-libusb.sh` (answers only libusb-1.0: cflags → the vendored
  headers, libs → empty); the real static target `usb-1.0` is linked directly,
  devourer before usb-1.0 (static archive order).
- Chip options match the fleet exactly, selected by `WBLINK_DEVOURER_CHIPS`:
  `fleet` (default) = JAGUAR1 (8812AU) + JAGUAR3_8822C (8812CU) +
  JAGUAR3_8822E (8812EU); `au` / `eu` / `8733b` pin one family for a craft
  build; `all` adds RTL8733BU to the fleet trio for a ground that may meet any
  craft. 8814/Jaguar2/Kestrel/PCIe are off in every combination, and the
  top-level CMake **fails** if the vendored tree builds a family that was not
  asked for.
